messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation did not lower depression scores compared with placebo in healthy women over winter.
Sentence: "We found no evidence of lower depression (P = 0·339), lower anxiety (P = 0·862), higher flourishing (P = 0·453), higher positive moods (P = 0·518) or lower negative moods (P = 0·538) in the treatment group compared with the control group at follow-up."
Measured as: depression (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale)
Population: 152 healthy women aged 18-40 years in Dunedin, New Zealand
Intervention: 50 000 IU oral vitamin D3 once per month for 6 months
Comparator: placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 152
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: In MDD patients, depression scores (BDI) decreased after three months of vitamin D3 supplementation.
Sentence: "After supplementation with vitamin D3 for three months, MDD patients showed improvements characterized by a decrease in their BDI's scores and an increase in their serum vitamin D and ghrelin concentrations."
Measured as: BDI score
Population: Patients with major depressive disorder (40 MDD patients; 32 healthy controls for baseline comparison)
Intervention: Vitamin D3 50,000 IU weekly for 3 months
Comparator: None (before vs after in a single group)
Design: case series
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
